subject: Approval request: AortaMed strategic discount and packaging restructure
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aortamed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing discussion for AortaMed pilot

Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and the exec team reviewed the preliminary commercial and asked if we can get to a more aggressive first-year effective rate. They flagged two constraints:

- AortaMed will commit to a 12-month pilot but needs unit economics to be defensible to the board (they asked for a lower per-token effective rate in year 1).
- They prefer a single packaged SKU (inference + private VPC add-on) with a consolidated invoice and a one-time onboarding credit.

Their informal ask: landing at ~30–35% off list for the first 12 months + a $60k onboarding credit. They’ve also suggested a higher minimum commit to make it palatable (> $900k).

Can Redwood make that work? Timing is tight — they want a signed SOW before December 1 to align with a board review.

Appreciate any flexibility.

—Elena
Head of Partnerships, AortaMed
Elena.Torres@aortamed.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aortamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing discussion for AortaMed pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. I spoke with the solutions team and pulled a revised package together (attached): consolidated SKU (inference + VPC), a 12-month pilot structure, and two commercial options:

Option A (Board-friendly): 30% off list year 1, $60k onboarding credit, $1.2M minimum commitment (12 months).
Option B (Conservative): 25% off list year 1, $30k onboarding credit, $900k minimum commitment.

We believe Option A is defensible only with the higher commit because of the private VPC upfront cost. I flagged this internally as outside of standard AE discount authority; I’m copying Marissa and Markus for approval.

Attached: aortamed_proposal_v3.pdf (commercial term sheet + redlines).

Ask: we need VP/CFO signoff for Option A. If that’s not available, we will propose Option B and keep the $60k onboarding credit as a negotiation leeway. Elena, if you can confirm which option the exec team prefers I’ll move to an updated SOW and DocuSign flow.

Timeline: need signoff by 11/18 to meet your Dec 1 SOW goal.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0128
Attachment: aortamed_proposal_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing discussion for AortaMed pilot — internal analysis

Priya / Markus —

I reviewed the proposal and ran a quick sensitivity on margin impact. Key points:

- Baseline list to Redwood realized margin (estimated): 45% gross margin on inference-only SKU. Private VPC increases one-time infra cost materially.
- Option A (30% + $60k credit, $1.2M commit) results in ~21–24% gross margin in year 1 assuming typical prefix caching and 10% usage overage. That’s below our comfort threshold for a new strategic account but acceptable if we secure the $1.2M ARR and a 12-month minimum with payment terms that reduce cash drag.
- Option B preserves ~27–30% margin with the $900k floor.

Recommended guardrails if we approve Option A:
- Require a 12-month minimum and prepayment for the first 3 months OR 60-day partial prepay schedule.
- Include a usage true-up at month 6 with the right to adjust pricing on renewal.
- Retain a “sunset clause”: the onboarding credit is non-recurring and tied to go-live within 90 days of SOW.

I attached a short sensitivity workbook. Please update the proposal to reflect the guardrails so legal can redline the SOW accordingly. If Markus (or Naomi) can provide the signoff language I’ll prepare the DocuSign packet and the revenue recognition note for RevOps.

> Elena —

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: financial-impact-sensitivities.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@aortamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-17T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing discussion for AortaMed pilot — internal analysis and sign-off

Priya / Elena —

Thanks for the context, team. After reviewing Marissa’s sensitivity and the strategic nature of AortaMed, I will approve Option A on a conditional basis. Conditions:

1) Customer signs a 12-month SOW with a $1.2M minimum contract value (MCV).
2) Redwood receives payment for months 1–3 as either upfront or within 60 days of invoice (finance to accept a 60-day partial prepay schedule).
3) Onboarding credit $60k is one-time, tied to go-live within 90 days, and not refundable.
4) Include a 6-month usage true-up and right to reprice on renewal if usage materially exceeds projected profiles.

Priya — please update the SOW to reflect those points and mark the commercial term sheet: “Approved by Markus Klein, VP Finance — conditional on payment and guardrails outlined.” Once updated, route to Naomi for FYI and to Legal for final redline. I will authorize DocuSign to proceed once the SOW contains the conditions above.

Elena — happy to move forward on this timeline; Priya will share the updated SOW by EOD 11/18 for your review.

Markus Klein
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Attachment: (none)
